AI-ConneX

Data Studio Compiler

Proof of Concept, Research Foundation & Technical Documentation

Agent-Assisted Heterogeneous Industrial Data Integration, Normalization and ValidationStage Report — Compiler / Data Preparation Layer

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-002-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler POC and Research Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: Performance | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DataStudioCompiler, CompilerResearch, PolarsEngine]

The AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler is an agent-assisted industrial data integration and normalization layer. Its purpose is to remove the manual burden of converting heterogeneous industrial datasets into a common structure before analytics, profiling and AI/ML workflows.

Industrial datasets may arrive as CSV, XLSX, JSON, TXT, Parquet, database exports and archives containing multiple files with different schemas. The Compiler discovers the input structure, extracts archives, identifies formats and schemas, determines whether files should be appended, joined, merged or retained separately, performs controlled transformations, normalizes units and timestamps where required, validates the result and produces lineage and a Compilation Report.

Central design principle: the agent recommends; the deterministic Compiler executes and validates. An LLM therefore does not directly modify industrial data.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-002-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler POC and Research Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: Performance | Section: 2. Problem Statement | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DataStudioCompiler, CompilerResearch, PolarsEngine]

Industrialists generally care about the engineering problem represented by their data, not about manually converting files or repairing schemas. Conventional preprocessing becomes expensive when datasets contain multiple formats, schema variants, units, timestamp conventions, duplicates, missing values, archives and schema drift.

AI-ConneX introduces a compilation stage between the natural-language Chatbot and the Data Profiler.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-002-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler POC and Research Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: Performance | Section: 3. Research Questions | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DataStudioCompiler, CompilerResearch, PolarsEngine]

Can an agent-assisted compiler automatically ingest heterogeneous industrial datasets and produce a validated unified representation?

Can the system determine when datasets should be appended, joined, merged, transformed or retained separately?

Can semantic/schema inference reduce manual column mapping effort?

Can deterministic validation detect data loss and transformation errors before downstream profiling?

Can transformation lineage make automated industrial data preparation auditable and reproducible?

AI-ConneX should not be positioned as inventing heterogeneous data integration, ETL, schema matching or data validation. The defensible contribution is their integration into an industrial, agent-assisted compilation workflow with explicit execution boundaries, validation and lineage.

The Compiler is therefore a domain-oriented compilation layer rather than merely a file converter.

section: 10. Key R&D Failures and AI-ConneX Responses
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-002-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler POC and Research Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: Performance | Section: 10. Key R&D Failures and AI-ConneX Responses | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DataStudioCompiler, CompilerResearch, PolarsEngine]



| Failure | Risk | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Format incompatibility | One parser cannot reliably read every format. | Format detection + dedicated readers + canonical intermediate representation. |
| ZIP contains unrelated files | Blind concatenation mixes unrelated tables. | Discover, classify and compare schemas before choosing operations. |
| Different names, same meaning | RPM, motor_speed and rotational_speed may be equivalent. | Schema matching using names, types, units, values, metadata and agent reasoning. |
| Same name, different meaning | Temperature may mean motor, oil, bearing or ambient temperature. | Require contextual evidence; names alone are insufficient. |
| Unit mismatch | 80 °C and 176 °F can be incorrectly treated as different values. | Detect/standardize units and record conversions. |
| Timestamp mismatch | Date formats/time zones can break joins and models. | Parse, normalize and retain timezone information where available. |
| Duplicates | Appending files can duplicate machine/time observations. | Candidate-key and configurable duplicate detection. |
| Schema drift | Later files may add/remove columns. | Schema-version detection and controlled evolution. |
| Corrupt tokens | ERROR, N/A or '-' can contaminate numeric fields. | Type-aware coercion with audit records. |
| Silent data loss | A pipeline may report success after dropping records. | Input/output balancing, rejection accounting and validation gates. |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-002-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler POC and Research Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: Performance | Section: 11. Reliability and Safety Principle | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DataStudioCompiler, CompilerResearch, PolarsEngine]

The fundamental rule is: Agent ≠ Compiler. The agent reasons about ambiguity; the Compiler owns execution. This separation enables deterministic validation, reproducibility and auditability.

LLM outputs must use a strict structured schema.

Transformations require validation before execution.

Low-confidence mappings should be routed for human review.

Source files remain immutable.

Every transformation is recorded in lineage.

Compiler failures are explicit; silent fallback is prohibited.

AI-ConneX proposes an agent-assisted industrial data compilation architecturethat combines deterministic heterogeneous-format ingestion, schema/semantic inference,transformation planning, automated validation and lineage generation into a unifiedpreprocessing stage designed for downstream industrial AI workflows.

This positions the work within established research on data integration, schema matching, ETL verification, data quality and semantic integration while identifying the AI-ConneX-specific contribution as the industrial compilation workflow and its execution/validation boundary.

[Governed Subsystems: DataStudioCompiler, CompilerResearch, PolarsEngine]

The Compiler is the controlled bridge between human intent and machine-ready industrial data. The Chatbot understands what the user wants; the Compiler determines and executes the data operations; the Data Profiler evaluates the resulting dataset; later AI-ConneX stages can therefore operate on a validated, traceable and reproducible data foundation.
